column1: # The "critical pure-core" class set of TASK-007: the logic that has no Android
# framework excuse for being untested, and the JVM test class that answers for it.
# Why an owner column exists at all: a line counter cannot tell a class that a
# test set out to exercise from one that happened to execute because something
# else called it. The owner is the single test class that carries this class
# past the floor with nothing else running, which is what
# verifyPureCoreAttribution re-measures. It is therefore the test responsible
# for the coverage, which is not always the test named after the class, and an
# owner is not a promise that the class has a test of its own.
# NONE means no single test class carries it: either nothing exercises the
# class at all, or its coverage is spread so thin across unrelated tests that
# none of them would be missed. That is a recorded gap, not a formality:
# verifyPureCoreCoverage fails on it until a test claims the class. Never
# invent an owner to silence the gate, and never record one that
# Not every class in a package the list reaches into belongs to it, so each
# one the check can see has to be judged once. verifyPureCoreCoverage watches
# every package that holds a listed class and fails on any class there that
# is neither listed nor excluded and has a branch or 20 lines. Without that,
# moving untested code into a new class in the same package would raise the
# aggregate instead of failing it. An exclusion records the judgement: which
# of the five membership rules in doc/testing-roadmap.md keeps the class out.
# Excluded classes are not measured, and an exclusion naming a class that is
# gone from the coverage reports, or that sits outside every watched
# package, fails the check as stale.
# A nested class declared in the source (Outer$Inner) is a class of its own
# and is judged on its own row, because membership is a question about each
# class. Code the compiler splits out of a class (lambdas, launch blocks and
# anonymous objects such as Outer$run$1, $$inlined$ copies, classes local to
# a function, WhenMappings, DefaultImpls) and the companion object, whatever
# it is named, are folded into the nearest declared class they came from, so
# Outer$Inner$run$1 counts as Outer$Inner. The gate tells the two apart from
# what the compiler recorded in each class file, not from the name;
# classFoldingOf in pure-core-coverage.gradle has the rule.
# Format: tab-separated, comments and blank lines ignored. Two row kinds:
#   Listed row, measured against the floors:
#     1. class         JaCoCo class name, slash form, no package-less shorthand.
#                      A declared nested class keeps its '$'; a generated one or
#                      a companion object is rejected. Top-level Kotlin functions live in the file
#     2. owner_test    fully qualified JVM test class, dot form, or NONE.
#     3. owner_module  Gradle path of the module holding owner_test, or - for NONE.
#   Excluded row, judged out of the set:
#     3. reason        a sentence naming the rule, as "rule N", and saying
#                      what about the class breaks it.
